immune_logic.have: K562 (leukemia), single unstimulated condition — no stimulus contrast, not an immune cell
immune_logic.proxy_caveat: this only finds BASAL regulators of an immune-gene panel in K562; it is NOT brakes-vs-gas (that requires the stimulus axis) and K562 does not mount an immune response.

verdict: Of the four canonical Perturb-seq applications, this K562 data cleanly supports ONE, gives a validated method-demo for another, and cannot honestly do the other two. [1] GRN WIRING DOES NOT (on this data): 4132 TF->TF influence edges were inferred, but they recover curated signed direct regulation at only 1.6x chance with 48% sign agreement (=chance), and the feed-forward loops are only 52% coherent — so this is a CO-RESPONSE network, not the causal wiring diagram. Why: a single bulk steady-state condition mixes direct+indirect (the 84%-unresolved result), and real GRN/FFL mapping needs time-resolved or nascent-RNA data to separate direct targets. The data property, not the idea, is the blocker. [2] UNKNOWN-GENE FUNCTION WORKS: fingerprint-kNN recovers a held-out known gene's pathway 84% (4.1x chance) and yields 128 confident dark-gene calls (TIMM23B~mito-import, GPN3~RNA-pol-assembly) — a validated similarity HINT, not proof, and it can be fooled by shared phenotype (a growth-arrest fingerprint looks alike regardless of mechanism). [3] DISEASE CONVERGENCE: the METHOD is validated hard (spliceosome positive control z=156.1), but it is thin here — only 1 disease has enough knocked-out risk genes and K562 is the wrong cell context for the neuro/immune diseases the application targets. [4] IMMUNE BRAKES-vs-GAS: NOT feasible — it needs a +/- stimulus axis and immune cells; this is a single unstimulated leukemia condition, so only basal regulators of an immune panel can be listed, a different and much weaker claim. Honest scorecard: one works, one is a validated hint, one is a method waiting for the right data, one is out of scope.
